stem: A nurse has previously passed fit testing for the N95 respirator model being used. After donning the respirator for patient care, what should the nurse do?

options.A: Skip any further fit-related check because annual fit testing is sufficient
options.B: Perform a user seal check each time the respirator is put on
options.C: Ask a coworker to confirm the seal by visual inspection alone
options.D: Remove the respirator and repeat formal fit testing before every use

rationale: OSHA requires a user seal check each time a tight-fitting respirator is put on, even after formal fit testing. The seal check uses the OSHA Appendix B-1 positive/negative pressure method or an equally effective manufacturer-recommended method; it is not a substitute for required fit testing.
educational_objective: Distinguish annual respirator fit testing from the user seal check that must be performed each time a tight-fitting respirator is donned.
source_document_title: 29 CFR 1910.134 Respiratory Protection; Appendix B-1 User Seal Check Procedures
source_claim_supported: Employees using tight-fitting respirators must perform a user seal check each time the respirator is put on using the specified or an effective manufacturer-recommended procedure.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
correction_summary: Replaced the oversimplified 'inhale and exhale sharply' technique with the exact OSHA requirement because seal-check technique varies by respirator and may use positive pressure, negative pressure, or manufacturer-approved methods.
audit_findings: B is the explicit OSHA requirement. A confuses fit testing with the per-use seal check; C is insufficient; D confuses the per-use seal check with formal fit testing. No second answer remains.
